data.raw_text: Crowds in Manila for the INC rally so far seem light, but it is a multi-day event, so crowd size is likely to increase before it's over. There is concern an effort to destabilize or overthrow the government of the Philippines may occur during the rallies. The organizers are allied with the Duterte clan and its membership is very loyal to the "church." They wield a lot of influence in the country politically. While this is not the first time rumors like this have been associated with prior similar events, the national mood in the Philippines has never before been so low in terms of dissatisfaction with the political system. The country has been rocked by evidence of historic amounts of corruption, which so far, have not yielded any high profile arrests. I believe, but have no evidence to back up my presumption, that this time those threats are a bit more credible. I believe the Marcos administration is also taking them more seriously as well. The same players tend to always be involved in these things- allegedly disgruntled retired general officers- but I have always suspected that what we hear about disgruntled retired officers is mostly bluster. The seriousness of the current corruption allegations make it possible that they're no longer just bluster. Using the rallies as a basis to incite broad civil unrest or disturbances that could serve as a distraction while a coup attempt is carried out appears to be the major security concern for the Presidential Security Group, the AFP and PNP.

The Manila Public Information Office (PIO) reported that an estimated 27,000 individuals gathered at Luneta Park and the Quirino Grandstand as of 11:00 a.m. on Sunday, November 16, for the Iglesia ni Cristo's Peaceful Rally for Transparency.

The figure was based on crowd monitoring by the Manila City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO).

📷 Manila Public Information Office
